title: dinky configuration
description: ~/.config/dinky/dinky.toml. Every key is optional; a key left out keeps its default.

start-at-login.description: Register dinky as a login item.

workspaces.description: Workspaces across all displays, numbered from 1, one native Space each. dinky creates and removes Spaces to match.

follow-space-order.description: Renumber workspaces when Spaces are reordered in Mission Control: on each display the leftmost Space becomes its lowest-numbered workspace, and windows stay put. False keeps each workspace's number and moves its windows back at the next arrangement.

workspace-to-display.description: By workspace number, the display it lives on: a pattern (main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `dinky list-displays` prints it) or a list of them, the first that matches a connected display winning. Other workspaces, and these when no pattern matches, live on the main display.

default-layout.description: Workspace layout. tiles is the original name for dwindle.

default-tiling.description: Whether dinky tiles numbered workspaces by default.

workspace.description: Tiling overrides for numbered workspaces on every display (1-based).

display.description: This workspace's settings while it is on one display, keyed by pattern: main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name. Omitted keys come from the workspace's own settings.

columns.description: Reserved columns for a fixed layout.

rows.description: Reserved rows for a fixed layout.

expand.description: Where overflow windows go when every fixed cell is full.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this workspace. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share on this workspace, over display and top-level values. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

follow-app-activation.description: When Cmd-Tab or a Dock click activates an app on another Space, switch there with the fast switch. A table also names apps not to follow.

exclude-apps.description: Bundle IDs whose activation is not followed, such as a menu bar app whose popover counts as a window.

float-windows-without-fullscreen.description: Float windows that can't go full screen, such as Finder's copy progress, About This Mac and Calculator. A `layout tiling` rule tiles one anyway.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width, inside the outer gaps, that a fullscreen window takes, centred. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set. Display and workspace tables override it.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share of the width inside the outer gaps. Workspace tables override display tables, which override this value. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

column-width.description: A new column's width as a share of the display. A lone column fills the display.

size.description: The master's share of the display inside the outer gaps while windows are stacked beside it. Hyprland calls it mfact.

side.description: The side the master takes; the stack goes on the other. Hyprland calls it orientation.

padding.description: Points by which neighbouring windows peek out.

orientation.description: What a container's orientation becomes when it switches to accordion: auto runs along its longer side, keep keeps the orientation it had.

display.description: Overrides for one display, keyed by pattern: main, secondary, or a case-insensitive part of the display's name as `dinky list-displays` prints it.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this display. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share on this display, over the top-level value. Workspace tables override it. If unset everywhere, uses the resolved fullscreen-width.

active-color.description: Colour of the focused window's border.

order.description: below draws the border directly below the window. above draws it above, as a ring that never covers the window's content or takes clicks.

exclude-apps.description: Bundle IDs whose windows get no border.

focus-follows-mouse.description: Focus the window under the pointer once the pointer rests on it.

delay-ms.description: How long the pointer must rest on a window before it takes focus. 0 focuses as soon as the pointer stops.

accordion-edges.description: Whether resting on the peeking edge of an accordion child focuses it.

animations.description: Windows glide to their tiles instead of jumping. Off while macOS's Reduce Motion is on.

duration-ms.description: Roughly how long a window takes to arrive. 0 jumps.

drag.description: Dragging a tiled window with the mouse.

placeholders.description: While you drag a tiled window, outline the tile it came from and the tile it will swap with.

split-trigger.description: What makes a drop split the tile instead of swapping: hold to rest the pointer on it for split-delay-ms, or a modifier key to hold.

split-delay-ms.description: With split-trigger = 'hold', how long the pointer must rest on the tile before the drop splits it.

modifiers.description: Which key of each modifier pair bindings answer to. The other key types as usual.

alt.description: Which Option key is alt in bindings.

ctrl.description: Which Control key is ctrl in bindings.

cmd.description: Which Command key is cmd in bindings.

shift.description: Which Shift key is shift in bindings.

hooks.description: dinky commands run on events. Shell goes through exec-and-forget.

startup.description: Once, when dinky starts, after it has read the windows and displays.

workspace-changing.description: As soon as dinky starts switching a display, and again when a burst of switches changes the target. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_WORKSPACE (the target), DINKY_PREV_WORKSPACE and DINKY_DISPLAY.

workspace-changed.description: Whenever a display's current workspace changes. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_WORKSPACE, DINKY_PREV_WORKSPACE and DINKY_DISPLAY.

focus-changed.description: When the focused window changes, debounced by 50 ms.

mode-changed.description: When the binding mode changes, including back to main when the config reloads. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_MODE and DINKY_PREV_MODE.

display-changed.description: When a display connects or disconnects. exec-and-forget gets DINKY_DISPLAYS and DINKY_PREV_DISPLAYS, how many displays there are now and were before.

rules.description: Rules for new windows. Every rule whose conditions all match runs, in order; for layout floating and layout tiling the last one wins.

app-id.description: The app's bundle ID, e.g. com.apple.Safari.

app-id-regex.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's bundle ID, e.g. ^com\.apple\. for every Apple app.

app-name.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the app's name.

title.description: Case-insensitive regex found anywhere in the window title.

run.description: The command or commands to run for a matching window.

mode.description: Key bindings, grouped in modes. dinky starts in main; the `mode <name>` command switches.

additionalProperties.description: Key combinations mapped to the command or commands they run.

gaps.description: Gaps in points. A side or axis left out keeps its default.

inner.description: Points between tiled windows: one value for both axes, or per axis.

outer.description: Points between tiled windows and the screen edge: one value, or per side.

command.description: A dinky command, as `dinky help` lists them: `workspace 3`, `layout floating`, `exec-and-forget open -a Safari`.

commands.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order.

columns.description: Reserved columns for a fixed layout.

rows.description: Reserved rows for a fixed layout.

expand.description: Where overflow windows go when every fixed cell is full.

fullscreen-width.description: The share of the width a fullscreen window takes on this workspace while it is on this display. Lone windows use it unless lone-window-width is set.

lone-window-width.description: A lone window's centred share while this workspace is on this display. Omitted values come from the workspace, then display and top-level settings, else the resolved fullscreen-width.

hook.description: A command or a list of commands, run in order. May be empty.

keyCombo.description: Zero or more modifiers (alt, ctrl, cmd, shift, or the shorthands hyper and meh) and one key name, joined by '-': alt-shift-h, ctrl-left, alt-page-up, hyper-1, f5.
